questions.question: If sinθ = 3x and cosθ = 3/x, (x ≠ 0) then the value of 6(x² + 1/x²) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sinθ = 3x and cosθ = 3/x, (x ≠ 0)

**Calculation:**

Sin²θ + cos²θ = (3x)² + (3/x)²

1 = 9(x² + 1/x²)

1/9 = (x² + 1/x²)

**∴ the value of 6(x² + 1/x²) = 6 × 1/9 = 2/3.**

According to the question,

questions.question: The distance between the centers of two circles of radii 4 cm, and 2 cm is 10 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The formula for the length of the **transverse common tangent (TCT)** is √(d² − (R + r)²).

Here, distance (d) = 10 cm, R = 4 cm, and r = 2 cm.

⇒ Sum of radii (R + r) = 4 + 2 = 6 cm.

⇒ Length of TCT = √(10² − 6²)

⇒ Length of TCT = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of 1st circle (R) = 4 cm

Radius of 2ⁿd circle (r) = 2 cm

Distance between centers (d) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of **transverse common tangent** = √[(Distance between centers)² − (Radius₁ + Radius₂)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/854cb7bf0359d25728114730c4e95491e2d35f425e3637c47471c6e0bbffb290.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of the **transverse common tangent** be L.

⇒ L = √[10² − (4 + 2)²]

⇒ L = √[100 − 6²]

⇒ L = √[100 − 36]

⇒ L = √64

⇒ L = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent is given by √[d² − (R − r)²], where circles lie on the same side of the tangent.

Existence of TCT

A transverse common tangent exists only if the distance between the centers (d) is greater than the sum of the radii (R + r).

Number of Common Tangents

If d > R + r, there are 4 common tangents (2 DCT and 2 TCT). If d = R + r, there are 3 common tangents.</p

questions.question: If each side of a rectangle is increased by 13%, then its area will increased by:
questions.solution:
**Calculation: **

Let the length and breadth of the rectangle both be 10 units.

Area of rectangle = L × B = 10 × 10 = 100 units

New length and breadth of the rectangle be = 10 + 10 × 13/100 = 11.3 units

New area of rectangle = 11.3 × 11.3 = 127.69 units

Percentage change = (127.69 - 100)/100 × 100 = 27.69%

**∴ The percentage change is 27.69%**

questions.question: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect externally at P. If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PB = 4 cm, then the length (in cm) of PC = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f45f21bcc1c41215d717d8f35f74660cf63f86e20fac5d248164dfd236fc9119.png] 

Using basic proportionality theorem,

PB × PA = PD × PC

⇒ 4 × 10 = PD × (PD + 3)

⇒ (PD)² + 3PD - 40 = 0

⇒ PD = 5 or - 8 

PC = CD + DP

PC = 3 + 5 = 8 cm

questions.question: If (x - 7)³ + (2x + 8)³ + (2x - 3)³ = 3(x - 7) (2x + 8) (2x - 3), then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(x - 7)3 + (2x + 8)3 + (2x - 3)3 = 3(x - 7) (2x + 8) (2x - 3) 

**Calculation: **

Let (x - 7), (2x + 8), and (2x - 3) be a, b, and c.

Now the equation can be written as,

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = 0

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c )(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - ac - bc)

⇒ (a + b + c) = 0

⇒ (x - 7) + (2x + 8) + (2x - 3) = 0

⇒ 5x = 2

**⇒ x = 0.4**

questions.question: What is the ratio of the number of students taken for all years together from school A to that from school B?
questions.solution:

The number of students taken for all years together from school B = (550 + 820 + 600 + 750 + 500 + 480) = 3700

questions.question: In which year, the percentage increase of students in school A is the highest in comparison to its previous year?
questions.solution:
The percentage increase in students in school A from year 2008-2009 = (800 – 640)/640 × 100 = 25%

The percentage decrease in students in school A from year 2009-2010 = (800 - 500)/800 × 100 = 37.5%

The percentage increase in students in school A from year 2010-2011 = (700 - 500)/500 × 100 = 40%

The percentage increase in students in school A from year 20011-2012 = (900 - 700)/700 × 100 = 28.57%

The percentage increase in students in school A from year 20012-2013 = (900 - 750)/900 × 100 = 16.66%

∴ The percentage increase of students in school A is the highest in comparison to its previous year 2011.

questions.question: What is the average of the number of students from school A during the six year period?
questions.solution: The average of the number of students from school A during the six year period = (640 + 800 + 500 + 700 + 900 + 750)/6 = 4290/6 = 715

questions.question: In which year, the absolute difference of the students in two schools is the lowest?
questions.solution:
The absolute difference of the students in two schools in year 2008 = 640 – 550 = 90

Difference between the numbers of students in year 2009 = 820 – 800 = 20

Difference between the numbers of students in year 2010 = 600 – 500 = 100

Difference between the numbers of students in year 2011 = 750 – 700 = 50

Difference between the numbers of students in year 2012 = 900 – 500 = 400

Difference between the numbers of students in year 2013 = 750 – 480 = 270

The absolute difference between the numbers of students in two schools is the lowest in year 2009.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They got a contract to complete the work for Rs. 35000. The share of B (in Rs.) in the contracted money will be:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM of the time taken by A and B.

Total work = 30

Efficiency = total work/time taken

Efficiency of A = 30/15 = 2 units/day

Efficiency of B = 30/10 = 3 units/day

The share was given in the ratio of their efficiencies = 2 : 3

(2 + 3) units = 35000

1 unit = 7000

**∴ B’s share = 3 × 7000 = 21000**

questions.question: Given n is an integer, what is the remainder when (6n + 3)² is divided by 9?
questions.solution:
**Calculation: **

Check using n = 1, 2, 3….. and so on.

Number = (6n + 3)² = (6 × 1 + 3)² = 81

**The remainder on dividing 81 by 9 is 0.**

questions.question: The average age of fifteen persons is 32 years. If two more persons are added then the average is increased by 3 years. The new persons have an age difference of 7 years between them. The age (in years) of the youngest among the new persons is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation: **

The average age of 15 persons = 32

Sum of age of 15 persons = 32 × 15 = 480

The average age of 17 persons = 32 + 3 = 35

Sum of age of 15 persons = 35 × 17 = 595

Sum of age of 2 new persons = 595 – 480 = 115

Difference of 2 new persons = 7

**∴ Age of youngest person = (115 – 7)/2 = 54**

questions.question: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 2 ∶ 5. If the first train runs 350 km in 5 hours, then the sum of the speed (in km/h) of both the trains is:
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The ratio between the speeds of two trains = 2 ∶ 5

Speed of 1st train = 350/5 = 70 km/hr

Speed of 2ⁿd train = 70 × 5/2 = 175 km/hr

**The sum of the speeds of the trains = 70 + 175 = 245 kmph**

questions.question: Two students, A and B, appeared for an examination. A secured 8 marks more than B and the marks of the former was 60% of the sum of their marks. The sum of the marks obtained by A and B is:
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Marks of A = Marks of B + 8

According to the Question,

A = (A + B) × 60/100

⇒ A – 3A/5 = 3B/5

⇒ 2A/5 = 3B/5

⇒ A/B = 3/2 = 3 : 2

Difference of marks = (3 - 2) = 1 unit = 8 marks

⇒ Sum of the marks (5 units) = 5 × 8 = 40 marks

**Sum of marks obtained by A and B = 40**

The sum of the salaries of A and B together is Rs. 43000. A spends 95% of his salary and B, 80% of his salary. If now their savings are the same, what is B’s salary (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of the salaries of A and B together is Rs. 43000

A's expenditure = 95% of his salary 

B's expenditure = 80% of his salary 

**Calculation:**

Let the salary of A be x.

Salary of B = 43000 – x

Saving of A = 100 – 95 = 5%

Saving of B = 100 – 80 = 20%

According to question,

x × 0.05 = (43000 – x) × 0.2

⇒ 0.25x = 8600

⇒ x = 34400

**∴ B’s salary = 43000 – 34400 = 8600**
